prompt: design antibody binders (single domain antibodies/nanobodies) against the ECL2 (extracellular loop 2) of LPAR1 and MRGPRX2 (both targets are GPCRs), with a high degree of accuracy

text:
I need to flag scope before spending budget on this.

**Two honesty checks up-front:**

1. **Antibody/nanobody design is out of scope for this pipeline.** Per `CLAUDE.md` and the skill: "Antibody-design content (RFantibody/ANARCI/IMGT, scFv/VHH) was removed — out of scope for the de-novo mini-binder pipeline." What I *can* design is **de novo mini-binders** (60–100 aa α-helical bundles, not Ig-fold VHHs with CDR loops). These are not nanobodies — they have no framework, no CDRs, and a different developability profile. If you need actual VHHs, this tool can't produce them; you'd want RFantibody or a library/display approach.

2. **GPCR ECL2 is one of the hardest target classes for de novo design.** ECL2 is a short, flexible loop, often partially unresolved in crystal/cryo-EM structures, and conformationally heterogeneous. Most published de novo binder successes are against rigid, well-folded surfaces (cytokines, hormone receptors' ectodomains, viral glycoproteins). I have no strong prior that the strict quality gate (complex pLDDT >93, ipSAE ≥0.93, iPTM ≥0.7, hotspot ≥0.70, BSA ≳700 Å²) is reachable against an ECL2 epitope of a GPCR within 4 rounds — the loop may not even present a stable enough surface for AF2-multimer to score confidently. Two targets in one run halves the per-target budget further.

**How would you like to proceed?**

questions.question: How should I scope this run given the constraints above?

options.label: De novo mini-binders, LPAR1 ECL2 only
options.description: Focus full 4-round budget on one target (LPAR1 ECL2). Mini-binders, not VHHs. Highest chance of a hit but still hard.

options.label: De novo mini-binders, MRGPRX2 ECL2 only
options.description: Focus full 4-round budget on MRGPRX2 ECL2. Same caveats.

options.label: Split budget across both GPCRs
options.description: 2 rounds each. Lower hit-rate per target; useful if you want comparative data.

options.label: Abort — I actually need true nanobodies
options.description: Stop now; this pipeline cannot produce Ig-fold VHHs. Recommend RFantibody or display-library workflows.

text: Awaiting your selection before I touch any tools.
